Jaṣa is the name of some aquatic animal or fish in the
Atharvaveda^1 and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.^2 The commentary
on the latter text explains it by makara, probably meaning
‘dolphin.’ The word also occurs in the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa.^3
Cf. Jhaṣa.
1) xi. 2, 25. There are various read-
ings: jhaṣa, jakha, jagha.
2) v. 5, 13, 1.
3) ii. 2, 5.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 96;
Whitney, Translation of the Atharva-
veda, 624

Jāṣkamada is the name of an unknown animal in the Athar-
vaveda.^1
1) xi. 9, 9. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 88.

Jās-pati occurs once in the Rigveda^1 in the sense of the
‘head of the family.’ The abstract formed from this word,
Jās-patya, apparently denoting ‘lordship of children,’ is also
found there.^2
1) i. 135. 8.
2) Rv. v. 28, 3; x. 85, 23.
